content.value_statement: Game projects need platform, engine, design, art, audio, and performance choices early. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to focused game development guidance for those decisions.
actual_capabilities: Routes projects to web, mobile, PC, VR/AR, 2D, 3D, design, art, audio, or multiplayer sub-skills.
Explains game loop, input abstraction, performance budget, AI selection, and collision strategy.
Compares game frameworks and engines for browser, desktop, console, mobile, and VR/AR projects.
Provides design guidance for core loops, GDD structure, progression, balancing, and player motivation.
Documents production guidance for assets, animation, audio categories, adaptive music, and platform constraints.
Covers multiplayer architecture, synchronization, lag compensation, server authority, and anti-cheat principles.
limitations: It provides principles and routing guidance, not complete runnable game projects.
It does not replace engine documentation, platform certification rules, or playtesting.
Some technology references may age and need verification before production choices.
It cannot validate performance, store compliance, or networking safety without project context.

use_cases.title: Plan an indie game prototype
use_cases.description: Choose the right sub-skills and first technical decisions for a small game concept.

use_cases.title: Structure a production design pass
use_cases.description: Organize guidance for core loops, progression, art direction, audio, and performance constraints.

use_cases.title: Review platform-specific tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare browser, mobile, PC, console, VR/AR, and multiplayer constraints before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan my game concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new game idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this game-development skill to choose the right sub-skills for a [platform] [genre] game. Summarize the first design and technical decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a platform and engine
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate selection before a prototype starts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the best platform and engine options for my [team size] team building [game type]. Include tradeoffs for performance, assets, and publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a performance plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a performance plan for a [2D or 3D] game targeting [hardware]. Include frame budget, asset strategy, input model, and profiling priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Review multiplayer architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for online game systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my multiplayer game concept for architecture, synchronization, lag compensation, server authority, and anti-cheat risks. Recommend the relevant sub-skills.

output: Start with framework choice, fixed timestep movement, sprite atlas planning, and level loop design.
Verify browser audio, asset loading, and mobile input constraints before production.

output_examples.input: Compare options for a multiplayer VR shooter.
output: Prioritize comfort, stable frame rate, server authority, and hit validation.
Prototype locomotion and networking early because both affect core design.

output_examples.input: Prepare art and audio direction for a mobile puzzle game.
output: Route to mobile-games, game-art, game-audio, and game-design.
Define touch-first interactions, readable art scale, lightweight audio formats, and puzzle progression.
Keep battery, file size, and store requirements in scope from the first prototype.

best_practices: Start with the core loop, then select platform and dimension guidance.
Verify engine, store, and browser details against current official documentation.
Pair this skill with prototypes, profiling data, and playtest feedback.
anti_patterns: Asking it to generate a complete shipped game with no target platform.
Treating static recommendations as final without testing on target hardware.
Mixing many sub-skill recommendations without a clear production priority.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It routes game projects to focused guidance for platforms, dimensions, design, art, audio, and multiplayer systems.

faq.question: Can it build a complete game by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning and implementation guidance that still needs engine work, testing, and iteration.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include platform store rules?
faq.answer: It includes high-level store and platform considerations, but current official requirements should be checked before release.

faq.question: Is it useful for multiplayer games?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes routing and guidance for architecture, synchronization, lag compensation, server authority, and anti-cheat principles.

faq.question: How should teams use the sub-skills?
faq.answer: Select the sub-skills that match the project first, then combine only the guidance that affects current production decisions.
